newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Resources takes 24.3 pct of Cosmos.
newsitem.headline: China Resources takes 24.3 pct of Cosmos.

text.p: Cosmos Machinery Enterprises Ltd said on Monday China Resources (Holdings) Co Ltd (CRC) would take 24.3 percent of the company following Cosmos' purchase of plastic machinery maker Welltec Industrial Equipment Ltd.
Cosmos said it had agreed to buy all of Welltec from Tai Tung Industrial Equipment Ltd for HK$272.9 million, with the purchase funded by an issue of 303.22 million new Cosmos shares at HK$0.90 each.
Tai Tung is 51 percent owned by Cosmos' parent Cosmos Holdings and 49 percent by CRC, the parent of China Resources Enterprise Ltd.
Cosmos said the purchase price was based on a price-earnings multiple of 7.5 times Welltec's combined audited profit of HK$36.4 million for the year ended in December 1996.
Cosmos also said it would issue 24.22 million new shares at HK$0.90 each to certain company directors to buy out their minority interests in a number of subsidiaries for HK$21.8 million.

In the third portion of the deal, Cosmos said it planned to place 81 million new shares at HK$0.90 each to the market, raising net proceeds of HK$70.8 million to cut its bank borrowings and for working capital.
On completion of the issue of the 408.44 million new shares, Cosmos Holdings' stake in Cosmos Machinery will be cut to 46 percent from 62.4 percent.
CRC, which now holds no interest in Cosmos Machinery, will own 24.3 percent of the company.

"The directors believe that the acquisitions will provide synergy with the group's existing business. The group will be able to better utilise the distribution and sales networks and to streamline the two operations," Cosmos said in the statement.

Cosmos also proposed to increase its authorised share capital to HK$400 million by creation of an additional 750 million new shares of HK$0.40 each, from the current HK$100 million divided into 250 million shares.
"The directors have no immediate intention of issuing any part of the authorised share capital of the company," it said.
Cosmos shares resumed trading on Monday after being suspended on Friday and were HK$0.57 higher at HK$1.88 in mid-morning.
